records.source: וַֽיִּגְּשׁ֗וּ רָאשֵׁי֙ אֲב֣וֹת הַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֶל־אֶלְעָזָר֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נ֑וּן וְאֶל־רָאשֵׁ֛י אֲב֥וֹת הַמַּטּ֖וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And approached [the] heads of [the] fathers of the Levites to Eleazar the priest and to Joshua son of Nun and to [the] heads of [the] fathers of the tribes of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: The family heads of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun and to the family heads of the tribes of Israel.

L.1: And the heads of the fathers of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.1: The leaders of the Levite families went to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun and to the leaders of the families in the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "House of the fathers" is the Hebrew name for an extended family traced through its male line; "heads of the fathers" is short for the heads of such families. The same leaders, with Eleazar and Joshua, shared out the land (14:1; 19:51).

decisions.choice: the Levites come to claim what Moses had commanded
decisions.reason: The land has now been divided among the tribes (chapters 14-19) and the cities of refuge named (chapter 20). The Levites, who received no territory of their own (13:14, 33; 14:3-4), come to ask for the towns promised them in Numbers 35:1-8.

decisions.choice: family heads (Balanced) / leaders of the families (Readable)
decisions.reason: The plain sense of the title, as in 14:1; Literal keeps the Hebrew form.

records.heading: Towns for the Levites

records.source: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם בְּשִׁלֹ֗ה בְּאֶ֤רֶץ כְּנַ֨עַן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה בְיַד־מֹשֶׁ֔ה לָֽתֶת־לָ֥נוּ עָרִ֖ים לָשָׁ֑בֶת וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶ֖ן לִבְהֶמְתֵּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And they spoke to them at Shiloh in [the] land of Canaan, saying, Yahweh commanded by [the] hand of Moses to give to us cities to dwell [in] and their pasture lands for our livestock.
pieces: They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded through Moses that we be given towns to live in, and their pasturelands for our livestock."

L.2: And they spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to dwell [in], and their pasturelands for our livestock."

R.2: At Shiloh in the land of Canaan they said to them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave a command through Moses. He said that we should be given towns to live in, and their pasturelands for our animals."

decisions.choice: Shiloh: where the tent of meeting stood
decisions.reason: Israel had set up the tent of meeting at Shiloh, and the last lots for the land were cast there before the LORD (18:1, 8-10; 19:51).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: The "hand" of a person is the means by which something is done. The LORD gave the command, and Moses was the one who passed it on.

decisions.choice: pasturelands: the open land around a town, kept for grazing
decisions.reason: The word names the common land just outside a town, used for the townspeople's herds and flocks, not for houses or crops (Numbers 35:2-5). The pasturelands of the Levites' towns could never be sold (Leviticus 25:34).

decisions.choice: the command of Numbers 35:1-8
decisions.reason: The LORD told Moses that the tribes were to give the Levites forty-eight towns with their pasturelands, more from the large tribes and fewer from the small (Numbers 35:1-8). This chapter tells how that was done.

decisions.choice: cities / towns; "X and its pasturelands" kept the same at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers places of any size; most of these were small walled settlements, so Balanced and Readable say "towns", as in 14:4. The phrase "and its pasturelands" repeats after every name in the lists that follow, and it is kept word for word the same each time so the list reads as the Hebrew does.

records.source: וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל לַלְוִיִּ֛ם מִנַּחֲלָתָ֖ם אֶל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֶת־הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֶת־מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And gave [the] sons of Israel to the Levites from their inheritance by [the] mouth of Yahweh the cities the these and their pasture lands.
pieces: So at the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave the Levites the following towns and their pasturelands out of their own inheritance.

L.3: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gave to the Levites from their inheritance, at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, these cities and their pasturelands.

R.3: So, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave the Levites some of their own land. They gave the towns listed below and their pasturelands.

decisions.choice: by the mouth of the LORD: at the LORD's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says. The tribes give up these towns because the LORD said so, not by their own choice alone.

decisions.choice: from their inheritance: out of the land each tribe had received
decisions.reason: The towns came out of the tribes' own lasting shares of the land, so each tribe gave up something of what it held.

decisions.choice: these cities: points ahead to the list
decisions.reason: "These" looks forward to the towns named in verses 9-40.

decisions.choice: the following / listed below
decisions.reason: Makes clear that "these" refers to the towns about to be named.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַגּוֹרָ֖ל לְמִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת הַקְּהָתִ֑י וַיְהִ֡י לִבְנֵי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֵ֜ן מִן־הַלְוִיִּ֗ם מִמַּטֵּ֣ה יְ֠הוּדָה וּמִמַּטֵּ֨ה הַשִּׁמְעֹנִ֜י וּמִמַּטֵּ֤ה בִנְיָמִן֙ בַּגּוֹרָ֔ל עָרִ֖ים שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And came out the lot for [the] clans of the Kohathites, and were for [the] sons of Aaron the priest, from the Levites, from [the] tribe of Judah and from [the] tribe of the Simeonite and from [the] tribe of Benjamin, by the lot, cities thirteen.
pieces: The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites. The descendants of Aaron the priest, who were among the Levites, received thirteen towns by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon and Benjamin.

L.4: And the lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites; and the sons of Aaron the priest, of the Levites, had from the tribe of Judah and from the tribe of the Simeonites and from the tribe of Benjamin, by lot, thirteen cities.

R.4: When lots were cast, one came out for the clans of Kohath. The descendants of Aaron the priest, who belonged to the Levites, received thirteen towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon and Benjamin.

decisions.choice: the Kohathites: one of the three Levite clan groups
decisions.reason: The Levites were descended from Levi's three sons, Gershon, Kohath and Merari (Numbers 3:17), and the chapter is ordered by these three groups. Aaron belonged to Kohath's line (Exodus 6:18-20), so his descendants, the priests, are listed first and apart from the other Kohathites.

decisions.choice: the lot came out: the share was decided by drawing lots
decisions.reason: As with the land itself, the towns were assigned by lot, so the outcome was left to the LORD rather than to the leaders' preference (Numbers 26:55-56; Proverbs 16:33).

decisions.choice: the tribe of the Simeonite: the tribe of Simeon
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew uses the clan name, "the Simeonite", in place of "Simeon"; it means the same tribe.

decisions.choice: descendants of Aaron
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the whole priestly line descended from Aaron, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants"; Literal keeps "sons".

records.source: וְלִבְנֵ֨י קְהָ֜ת הַנּוֹתָרִ֗ים מִמִּשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת מַטֵּֽה־אֶ֠פְרַיִם וּֽמִמַּטֵּה־דָ֞ן וּמֵחֲצִ֨י מַטֵּ֧ה מְנַשֶּׁ֛ה בַּגּוֹרָ֖ל עָרִ֥ים עָֽשֶׂר׃ס
records.gloss: And for [the] sons of Kohath the remaining, from [the] clans of [the] tribe of Ephraim and from [the] tribe of Dan and from [the] half of [the] tribe of Manasseh, by the lot, cities ten.
pieces: The rest of the descendants of Kohath received ten towns by lot from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan and from the half-tribe of Manasseh.

L.5: And the rest of the sons of Kohath [had] from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim and from the tribe of Dan and from the half of the tribe of Manasseh, by lot, ten cities.

R.5: The rest of Kohath's descendants received ten towns from the tribes of Ephraim and Dan and from half the tribe of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: the remaining: the Kohathites who were not descended from Aaron
decisions.reason: Verse 4 dealt with the priests; "the rest" are the other Kohathite families, who served at the sanctuary but were not priests (Numbers 4:1-15).

decisions.choice: the half of the tribe of Manasseh: here the half west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Manasseh's land lay on both sides of the Jordan (13:29-31; 17:1-13). The towns given from it in verse 25, Taanach and Gath-rimmon, are in the western half.

decisions.choice: received
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb ("to the sons of Kohath ... ten cities"); "received" supplies it, as "had" does in brackets at Literal.

records.source: וְלִבְנֵ֣י גֵרְשׁ֗וֹן מִמִּשְׁפְּח֣וֹת מַטֵּֽה־יִשָּׂשכָ֣ר וּמִמַּטֵּֽה־אָ֠שֵׁר וּמִמַּטֵּ֨ה נַפְתָּלִ֜י וּ֠מֵחֲצִי מַטֵּ֨ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה בַבָּשָׁן֙ בַּגּוֹרָ֔ל עָרִ֖ים שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And for [the] sons of Gershon, from [the] clans of [the] tribe of Issachar and from [the] tribe of Asher and from [the] tribe of Naphtali and from [the] half of [the] tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, by the lot, cities thirteen.
pieces: The descendants of Gershon received thirteen towns by lot from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, from the tribes of Asher and Naphtali and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.

L.6: And the sons of Gershon [had] from the clans of the tribe of Issachar and from the tribe of Asher and from the tribe of Naphtali and from the half of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, by lot, thirteen cities.

R.6: Gershon's descendants received thirteen towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher and Naphtali and from half the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.

decisions.choice: Bashan: the land east of the Jordan and north of Gilead
decisions.reason: Bashan was the kingdom of Og that Moses gave to half the tribe of Manasseh (13:29-31). With it, the Gershonites' towns all lie in the north of the land.

decisions.choice: for the sons of Gershon: the second Levite clan group
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the Hebrew has no verb; the towns belonged to them by lot.

records.source: לִבְנֵ֨י מְרָרִ֜י לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֗ם מִמַּטֵּ֨ה רְאוּבֵ֤ן וּמִמַּטֵּה־גָד֙ וּמִמַּטֵּ֣ה זְבוּלֻ֔ן עָרִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵֽה׃
records.gloss: For [the] sons of Merari according to their clans, from [the] tribe of Reuben and from [the] tribe of Gad and from [the] tribe of Zebulun, cities twelve.
pieces: The descendants of Merari, clan by clan, received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.

L.7: For the sons of Merari according to their clans [were] from the tribe of Reuben and from the tribe of Gad and from the tribe of Zebulun twelve cities.

R.7: Merari's descendants, clan by clan, received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.

decisions.choice: Merari: the third Levite clan group
decisions.reason: Reuben and Gad lay east of the Jordan and Zebulun in the north. The twelve towns are listed in verses 34-39, four from each tribe.

decisions.choice: according to their clans: clan by clan
decisions.reason: The towns were shared out among the separate clans of Merari's line (Numbers 3:33).

records.source: וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֶת־הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֶת־מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה בַּגּוֹרָֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And gave [the] sons of Israel to the Levites the cities the these and their pasture lands, as commanded Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses, by the lot.
pieces: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave these towns and their pasturelands to the Levites by lot, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses.

L.8: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gave to the Levites these cities and their pasturelands, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded by the hand of Moses, by lot.

R.8: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} used lots to give these towns and their pasturelands to the Levites. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses.

decisions.choice: a summary that closes the overview
decisions.reason: Verses 4-7 give the totals for each group; this verse sums them up, repeating verse 3, before the towns are named one by one from verse 9.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּ מִמַּטֵּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּמִמַּטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֑וֹן אֵ֚ת הֶֽעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָ֥א אֶתְהֶ֖ן בְּשֵֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And they gave from [the] tribe of [the] sons of Judah and from [the] tribe of [the] sons of Simeon the cities the these which one called them by name.
pieces: From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they gave the towns that are named below.

L.9: And they gave from the tribe of the sons of Judah and from the tribe of the sons of Simeon these cities that are [here] called by name.

R.9: From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they gave the towns that are named here.

decisions.choice: which one called by name: which are mentioned by name
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject ("he called"); it is an impersonal way of saying that the towns are about to be listed by name.

decisions.choice: the tribe of the sons of Judah: the tribe of Judah
decisions.reason: "Sons of Judah" here is the tribe as a whole. Simeon's land lay inside Judah's (19:1, 9), which is why the two are counted together.

decisions.choice: named below / named here
decisions.reason: The plain sense of the impersonal phrase.

records.heading: The towns of Aaron’s descendants

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ לִבְנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן מִמִּשְׁפְּח֥וֹת הַקְּהָתִ֖י מִבְּנֵ֣י לֵוִ֑י כִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם הָיָ֥ה הַגּוֹרָ֖ל רִיאשֹׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was for [the] sons of Aaron, from [the] clans of the Kohathite, from [the] sons of Levi, for to them was the lot first.
pieces: They went to the descendants of Aaron, who belonged to the Kohathite clans among the Levites, because the first lot fell to them.

L.10: And [they] were for the sons of Aaron, of the clans of the Kohathites, of the sons of Levi, for theirs was the first lot.

R.10: These towns went to Aaron's descendants, who were part of the Kohathite clans of the Levites. Their lot was the first one drawn.

decisions.choice: it was: these towns belonged
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "it was for the sons of Aaron"; the subject is the towns named in verse 9.

decisions.choice: the first lot was theirs
decisions.reason: The priests' share was drawn first, which explains why they are listed first. The Hebrew can also be read "for the lot was theirs first"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: They went / These towns went
decisions.reason: Supplies the subject the Hebrew leaves to the context.

records.source: וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ לָהֶ֜ם אֶת־קִרְיַת֩ אַרְבַּ֨ע אֲבִ֧י הָֽעֲנ֛וֹק הִ֥יא חֶבְר֖וֹן בְּהַ֣ר יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֖הָ סְבִיבֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And they gave to them Kiriath-arba, father of the Anak, that [is] Hebron, in [the] hill country of Judah, and its pasture lands around it.
pieces: They gave them Kiriath-arba (Arba was the father of Anak), that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, and its pasturelands around it.

L.11: And they gave them Kiriath-arba, [Arba being] the father of the Anak, that [is] Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, and its pasturelands around it.

R.11: They gave them Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, and its pasturelands around it. The town's old name came from Arba, the father of Anak.

decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba: the old name of Hebron
decisions.reason: The name means "town of Arba". Joshua 14:15 and 15:13 explain that Arba was the greatest of the Anakim, and that the town later called Hebron was named after him.

decisions.choice: father of the Anak: Arba was the ancestor of the Anakim
decisions.reason: The phrase describes Arba, not the town. The Anakim were the tall people whom the spies feared (Numbers 13:22, 28, 33) and whom Caleb drove out of Hebron (15:14).

decisions.choice: its pasturelands around it
decisions.reason: Only here and in verse 42 does the list add "around it", making clear that the town's grazing land surrounded it on every side (Numbers 35:4-5).

decisions.choice: (Arba was the father of Anak)
decisions.reason: Supplies the words that show the phrase describes the man Arba; Literal shows them in brackets.

records.source: וְאֶת־שְׂדֵ֥ה הָעִ֖יר וְאֶת־חֲצֵרֶ֑יהָ נָֽתְנ֛וּ לְכָלֵ֥ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֖ה בַּאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] field of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh in his possession.
pieces: But the fields of the town and its villages they had already given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his own property.

L.12: But the field of the city and its villages they had given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.

R.12: But the farmland of the town and the villages around it had already been given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his own.

decisions.choice: but ... they had given: an earlier gift, set against verse 11
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the field of the city" first, setting it against the town and pasturelands just given to the priests. The gift to Caleb was made earlier (14:13-14; 15:13), so the verb is read as "had given".

decisions.choice: the field of the city and its villages: the farmland and outlying settlements
decisions.reason: The priests received the town itself and its common grazing land; the fields farther out and the small unwalled settlements that belonged to Hebron stayed with Caleb and his family. Both gifts stood side by side.

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: Brings out that the gift to Caleb had been made before this one.

records.source: וְלִבְנֵ֣י׀אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֗ן נָֽתְנוּ֙ אֶת־עִיר֙ מִקְלַ֣ט הָרֹצֵ֔חַ אֶת־חֶבְר֖וֹן וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֑הָ וְאֶת־לִבְנָ֖ה וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶֽׁהָ׃
records.gloss: And to [the] sons of Aaron the priest they gave [the] city of refuge [for] the killer, Hebron and its pasture lands, and Libnah and its pasture lands,
pieces: To the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave the city of refuge for anyone who had killed someone, Hebron and its pasturelands, along with Libnah and its pasturelands,

L.13: And to the sons of Aaron the priest they gave the city of refuge for the killer, Hebron and its pasturelands, and Libnah and its pasturelands,

R.13: To the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron and its pasturelands. Hebron was a town of safety, where a person who had killed someone could run for protection. They also gave them Libnah and its pasturelands.

decisions.choice: the city of refuge: Hebron, named in 20:7
decisions.reason: Hebron was one of the six cities set apart in chapter 20 for a person who had killed someone without intending to. All six were Levite towns, as Numbers 35:6 commanded; they are named again in this chapter (verses 21, 27, 32, 38, and Bezer in verse 36).

decisions.choice: the killer: one who has taken a human life
decisions.reason: The word names anyone who has killed a person. In the setting of the cities of refuge it means one who killed by accident and fled for protection until his case was heard (20:3-6).

decisions.choice: one sentence through verse 16
decisions.reason: The list of the nine towns from Judah and Simeon runs from here to the end of verse 16.

decisions.choice: anyone who had killed someone (Balanced); town of safety (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 35: Balanced spells out "the killer" as one who has killed someone, and Readable says "town of safety" for "city of refuge".

records.source: וְאֶת־יַתִּר֙ וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֔הָ וְאֶת־אֶשְׁתְּמֹ֖עַ וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶֽׁהָ׃
records.gloss: And Jattir and its pasture lands, and Eshtemoa and its pasture lands,
pieces: Jattir and its pasturelands, Eshtemoa and its pasturelands,

L.14: and Jattir and its pasturelands, and Eshtemoa and its pasturelands,

R.14: They also gave Jattir and its pasturelands, and Eshtemoa and its pasturelands.

decisions.choice: Jattir and Eshtemoa: towns in the hill country of Judah
decisions.reason: Both are named among Judah's hill towns in 15:48 and 15:50 (Eshtemoa there spelled Eshtemoh). The list continues from verse 13.

decisions.choice: the city of refuge: Golan, named in 20:8

records.gloss: And for [the] clans of [the] sons of Merari, the Levites the remaining, from [the] tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam and its pasture lands, Kartah and its pasture lands,
pieces: To the clans of the descendants of Merari, the rest of the Levites, they gave from the tribe of Zebulun Jokneam and its pasturelands, Kartah and its pasturelands,

L.34: And to the clans of the sons of Merari, the rest of the Levites, from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam and its pasturelands, Kartah and its pasturelands,

R.34: The clans of Merari's descendants were the rest of the Levites. From the tribe of Zebulun they received Jokneam and its pasturelands, and Kartah and its pasturelands.

decisions.choice: the remaining: the last of the Levite groups
decisions.reason: With the priests, the other Kohathites and the Gershonites provided for, Merari's clans are "the rest" of the Levites.

decisions.choice: Jokneam: a royal Canaanite town on Zebulun's border
decisions.reason: Its king is in the list of defeated kings (12:22), and it marks Zebulun's border (19:11).

decisions.choice: they gave
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb; Readable says "they received".

records.heading: The towns of Merari’s descendants

records.source: אֶת־דִּמְנָה֙ וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֔הָ אֶֽת־נַהֲלָ֖ל וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֑הָ עָרִ֖ים אַרְבַּֽע׃
records.gloss: Dimnah and its pasture lands, Nahalal and its pasture lands: cities four.
pieces: Dimnah and its pasturelands, and Nahalal and its pasturelands: four towns.

L.35: Dimnah and its pasturelands, Nahalal and its pasturelands: four cities.

R.35: They also received Dimnah and its pasturelands, and Nahalal and its pasturelands. That made four towns.

decisions.choice: Dimnah and Nahalal: towns of Zebulun
decisions.reason: Nahalal is in Zebulun's lot (19:15). Dimnah is not named elsewhere; it may be the Rimmon of 19:13, which 1 Chronicles 6:62 lists among Merari's towns.

records.source: וּמִמַּטֵּ֣ה רְאוּבֵ֔ן אֶת־בֶּ֖צֶר וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֑הָ וְאֶת־יַ֖הְצָה וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶֽׁהָ׃
records.gloss: And from [the] tribe of Reuben, Bezer and its pasture lands, and Jahaz and its pasture lands,
pieces: From the tribe of Reuben they gave Bezer and its pasturelands, Jahaz and its pasturelands,

L.36: And from the tribe of Reuben, Bezer and its pasturelands, and Jahaz and its pasturelands,

R.36: From the tribe of Reuben they received Bezer and its pasturelands, and Jahaz and its pasturelands.

decisions.choice: verses 36-37 are read as part of the text
decisions.reason: The Leningrad Codex, the manuscript on which the printed Hebrew text is based, does not have verses 36-37; it goes straight from Zebulun's towns to Gad's. The verses are found in many other Hebrew manuscripts and in the ancient Greek translation, which also calls Bezer "the city of refuge for the killer" and places it "in the wilderness" (as 20:8 and Deuteronomy 4:43 do). The same four towns stand in the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 6:63-64. Without them Merari's towns would number eight, not the twelve of verses 7 and 40, and the total would fall short of the forty-eight of verse 41. They are included, as the edition used here prints them. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence.

decisions.choice: Bezer: a city of refuge
decisions.reason: Bezer was the southern city of refuge east of the Jordan (20:8; Deuteronomy 4:43). Unlike the other five, it is not called a city of refuge in the Hebrew of this verse.

decisions.choice: Jahaz: where Israel defeated Sihon
decisions.reason: Jahaz is where Sihon king of Heshbon fought Israel and was defeated (Numbers 21:23-24); it is listed in Reuben's land in 13:18.

decisions.choice: they gave / they received
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.source: אֶת־קְדֵמוֹת֙ וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֔הָ וְאֶת־מֵיפָ֖עַת וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֑הָ עָרִ֖ים אַרְבַּֽע׃ס
records.gloss: Kedemoth and its pasture lands, and Mephaath and its pasture lands: cities four.
pieces: Kedemoth and its pasturelands, and Mephaath and its pasturelands: four towns.

L.37: Kedemoth and its pasturelands, and Mephaath and its pasturelands: four cities.

R.37: They also received Kedemoth and its pasturelands, and Mephaath and its pasturelands. That made four towns.

decisions.choice: part of the passage missing from the Leningrad Codex
decisions.reason: See the note on verse 36.

decisions.choice: Kedemoth and Mephaath: towns of Reuben
decisions.reason: Both are in Reuben's land (13:18). Moses sent messengers to Sihon from the wilderness of Kedemoth (Deuteronomy 2:26).

records.source: וּמִמַּטֵּה־גָ֗ד אֶת־עִיר֙ מִקְלַ֣ט הָרֹצֵ֔חַ אֶת־רָמֹ֥ת בַּגִּלְעָ֖ד וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֑הָ וְאֶֽת־מַחֲנַ֖יִם וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶֽׁהָ׃
records.gloss: And from [the] tribe of Gad, [the] city of refuge [for] the killer, Ramoth in Gilead and its pasture lands, and Mahanaim and its pasture lands,
pieces: From the tribe of Gad they gave the city of refuge for anyone who had killed someone, Ramoth in Gilead and its pasturelands, along with Mahanaim and its pasturelands,

L.38: And from the tribe of Gad, the city of refuge for the killer, Ramoth in Gilead and its pasturelands, and Mahanaim and its pasturelands,

R.38: From the tribe of Gad they gave Ramoth in Gilead and its pasturelands. Ramoth was a town of safety for a person who had killed someone. They also gave Mahanaim and its pasturelands.

decisions.choice: the city of refuge: Ramoth in Gilead, named in 20:8
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: Mahanaim: on the border of Gad and Manasseh
decisions.reason: Jacob named the place after meeting angels there (Genesis 32:3); it marks the edge of Gad's land (13:26, 30).

decisions.choice: they gave
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.source: אֶת־חֶשְׁבּוֹן֙ וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֔הָ אֶת־יַעְזֵ֖ר וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֑הָ כָּל־עָרִ֖ים אַרְבַּֽע׃
records.gloss: Heshbon and its pasture lands, Jazer and its pasture lands: all [the] cities four.
pieces: Heshbon and its pasturelands, and Jazer and its pasturelands: four towns in all.

L.39: Heshbon and its pasturelands, Jazer and its pasturelands: in all four cities.

R.39: They also gave Heshbon and its pasturelands, and Jazer and its pasturelands. That made four towns in all.

decisions.choice: Heshbon and Jazer: towns east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Heshbon had been Sihon's royal city (12:2); Jazer is named in Gad's land (13:25). Both lay in the land Moses took from Sihon.

records.source: כָּל־הֶ֨עָרִ֜ים לִבְנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔ם הַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים מִמִּשְׁפְּח֣וֹת הַלְוִיִּ֑ם וַיְהִי֙ גּוֹרָלָ֔ם עָרִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵֽה׃
records.gloss: All the cities for [the] sons of Merari according to their clans, the remaining from [the] clans of the Levites; and was their lot cities twelve.
pieces: All the towns given to the descendants of Merari, clan by clan, the rest of the Levite clans, came by lot to twelve towns.

L.40: All the cities for the sons of Merari according to their clans, the rest of the clans of the Levites: their lot was twelve cities.

R.40: So the clans of Merari's descendants, the last of the Levite clans, received twelve towns in all by lot.

decisions.choice: twelve: four each from Zebulun, Reuben and Gad
decisions.reason: The total matches verse 7 and counts Reuben's four towns in verses 36-37.

decisions.choice: their lot: the share that fell to them by lot
decisions.reason: "Lot" here stands for the share the lot assigned, as in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the last of the Levite clans
decisions.reason: "The rest" means the group that remained after the others had received their towns.

records.source: כֹּ֚ל עָרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עָרִ֛ים אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶ֖ה וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: All [the] cities of the Levites in [the] midst of [the] possession of [the] sons of Israel: cities forty and eight, and their pasture lands.
pieces: In all, the Levites had forty-eight towns and their pasturelands within the land held by the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.41: All the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel [were] forty-eight cities and their pasturelands.

R.41: The Levites had forty-eight towns and their pasturelands in all, spread out through the land that belonged to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: forty-eight: the number the LORD commanded
decisions.reason: The total matches Numbers 35:7: the six cities of refuge and forty-two others. Thirteen went to the priests, ten to the other Kohathites, thirteen to the Gershonites and twelve to the Merarites.

decisions.choice: in the midst of the possession: among all the tribes
decisions.reason: The Levites had no territory of their own but lived in towns scattered among every tribe's land, so that the tribe set apart to serve the LORD lived among all Israel (Genesis 49:7; Deuteronomy 33:10).

decisions.choice: spread out through
decisions.reason: Brings out "in the midst of": the towns lay among the lands of all the tribes.

records.source: תִּֽהְיֶ֨ינָה֙ הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה עִ֣יר עִ֔יר וּמִגְרָשֶׁ֖יהָ סְבִיבֹתֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֖ן לְכָל־הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ס
records.gloss: Were the cities the these city city and its pasture lands around it; so for all the cities the these.
pieces: Each of these towns had its pasturelands around it; it was the same for all of these towns.

L.42: These cities were each city [with] its pasturelands around it; so [it was] for all these cities.

R.42: Every one of these towns had pasturelands around it. This was true for all of them.

decisions.choice: city city: each city
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun gives the sense "every single one". The verse sums up that the grant was the same everywhere: a town together with the grazing land that surrounded it.

decisions.choice: its pasturelands around it
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לָתֵ֣ת לַאֲבוֹתָ֑ם וַיִּרָשׁ֖וּהָ וַיֵּ֥שְׁבוּ בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And gave Yahweh to Israel all the land which he swore to give to their fathers, and they took possession of it and dwelt in it.
pieces: In this way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel the whole land that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sworn to give to their ancestors, and they took possession of it and settled there.

L.43: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to Israel all the land which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sworn to give to their fathers; and they took possession of it and dwelt in it.

R.43: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel all the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised with an oath to give their ancestors. They took it over and made their homes there.

decisions.choice: which he swore to give to their fathers
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised the land on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 12:7; 15:18; 26:3; Exodus 6:8; Deuteronomy 1:8). These closing verses (43-45) look back over the whole book: the promise has been kept.

decisions.choice: all the land: the promise fulfilled, though some places were still unconquered
decisions.reason: The book itself says that land remained to be taken and that some Canaanites still lived among the tribes (13:1-6; 15:63; 16:10; 17:12). The summary speaks of the LORD's side: he gave what he had promised, and Israel's task was to take hold of it (23:4-5).

decisions.choice: took possession of: took the land as their own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over land and hold it, often by driving out those who held it before.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the forefathers of the nation, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

records.heading: Not one good promise failed

records.source: וַיָּ֨נַח יְהוָ֤ה לָהֶם֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לַאֲבוֹתָ֑ם וְלֹא־עָ֨מַד אִ֤ישׁ בִּפְנֵיהֶם֙ מִכָּל־אֹ֣יְבֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֹ֣יְבֵיהֶ֔ם נָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And gave rest Yahweh to them all around, according to all that he swore to their fathers; and not stood a man against them of all their enemies; all their enemies gave Yahweh into their hand.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave them rest all around them, in keeping with everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sworn to their ancestors. Not one of all their enemies could stand against them; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed all their enemies over to them.

L.44: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them rest all around, according to all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sworn to their fathers; and not a man of all their enemies stood before them; all their enemies {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave into their hand.

R.44: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave them rest and safety on every side, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised their ancestors with an oath. None of their enemies was able to stand up to them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave them victory over all their enemies.

decisions.choice: gave them rest: freedom from war and from the threat of enemies
decisions.reason: Rest in the land was what the LORD had promised (Deuteronomy 12:9-10; 25:19; Joshua 1:13, 15). It meant settled life without attack, the goal of the journey from Egypt.

decisions.choice: not a man stood before them: no one could resist them
decisions.reason: To "stand before" an enemy is to hold one's ground against him. The words echo the promise of 1:5.

decisions.choice: gave into their hand: gave them victory over
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power: the enemies were put into Israel's power.

decisions.choice: rest and safety
decisions.reason: Adds "safety" to bring out what this rest was: freedom from attack.

records.source: לֹֽא־נָפַ֣ל דָּבָ֔ר מִכֹּל֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַטּ֔וֹב אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הַכֹּ֖ל בָּֽא׃פ
records.gloss: Not fell a word from all the word the good which spoke Yahweh to [the] house of Israel; the all came.
pieces: Of all the good promises {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made to the house of Israel, not one failed; every one of them was fulfilled.

L.45: Not a word fell of all the good word which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to the house of Israel; all [of it] came.

R.45: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had made many good promises to the people of Israel. He did not fail to keep a single one. Every one of them happened.

decisions.choice: fell: failed, came to nothing
decisions.reason: A word that "falls" is one that is not carried out. The same saying returns at 23:14 and in Solomon's prayer (1 Kings 8:56).

decisions.choice: the good word: the LORD's promises of good
decisions.reason: "Word" here means what the LORD had said he would do for Israel: the land, rest and victory of verses 43-44.

decisions.choice: all came: all came true
decisions.reason: The verb "come" used of a promise means that it happened.

decisions.choice: promises
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what the "word" was; Literal keeps "word".

decisions.choice: He did not fail to keep a single one
decisions.reason: Readable puts the LORD as the subject to make the plain sense clear: every promise he made, he kept.
